newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Bonds ended an active day firmer on Tuesday breaching technical levels which some dealers said pointed to further gains on Wednesday.
At the 1400 GMT finish, the benchmark R150 stock was pegged at a 15.23 percent yield compared with 15.33 percent overnight.
The market was initially buoyed by the rand's continued stability as well as gains on the U.S. Treasury bond market overnight.
The R150 then steadily declined to its intraday low of 15.20 percent by midday amid good institutional interest, and held a tight range in the afternoon of 15.205 percent to 15.22 percent.
Dealers said that the R150's finish below the 15.25 percent level indicated that the stock could stage an assault on the 15.00 percent level this week.
"Technically speaking we have broken some good levels," a dealer said. "The close below 15.25 percent could be the start of a bull run."
Other traders were less optimistic that the market could extend its gains from current levels because such a move was not supported by fundamentals.
Dealers also voiced concern about the continuing high money market shortage which surged 850 million rand to 9.123 billion rand on Monday.

Andre Kock, head of money markets at the central Reserve Bank, played down the concerns about the rise in the shortage, attributing its spike to foreign exchange flows. Kock added that the shortage was expected to ease again over the next two days.

Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net sellers of 73.64 million rand of South African bonds on Monday after selling 136.898 million rand on Friday.Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at a meagre 2.24 billion rand from 4.46 billion on Friday.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.90 and 16.10 percent, while 90-day BAs were also unmoved at between 15.35 to 15.50 percent.
The rand held in a tight range on the day as market attention focused on the U.S. dollar's return to form.
It ended steady at 4.4900/4950 on the dollar from 4.4930/4980 overnight.
"Initially there were a couple of offers which pushed it lower, but there is demand below 4.49 which held it there for most of the day," a dealer said.
The dollar jumped over the psychological 1.50 marks hurdle earlier on comments out of Germany in support of a stronger dollar and indicating scope for further repo rate cuts, dealers said.

Traders said that in the face of an advancing dollar, third currencies retreated against the rand. It was last pegged at 6.9878/7.0001 against sterling from 7.0041/0164 on Monday and at 0.3352/3357 marks from 0.3315/3320 marks previously.
